knowledge_point.title: Sketching the Solution Curves of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x^{2}}?$ for $x>0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =1\int x^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =1\left(-x^{-1}\right)+C \\ y & =- \frac{1}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$ for $x>0$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=2 x + 4?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2 x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =2\int x + 2\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\left(\frac{\left(x + 2\right)^{2}}{2}\right)+C \\ y & =\left(x + 2\right)^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096698/plots/a5beb48275164e76d796c1ef67635e0ab25d1b205110568bb85fb8ae0981cad5.png)

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- 3 \left(x - 1\right)^{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (- 3 \left(x - 1\right)^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =-3\int \left(x - 1\right)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\left(\frac{\left(x - 1\right)^{3}}{3}\right)+C \\ y & =- \left(x - 1\right)^{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- \frac{9 \left(x - 1\right)^{2}}{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (- \frac{9 \left(x - 1\right)^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =- \frac{9}{2}\int \left(x - 1\right)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =- \frac{9}{2}\left(\frac{\left(x - 1\right)^{3}}{3}\right)+C \\ y & =- \frac{3 \left(x - 1\right)^{3}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096698/plots/06a95cfedf2b19426726fe67fd97b19ffa8ee557b206fc64014d025af8bebe39.png)

question.:question/problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- \frac{9 e^{- \frac{3 x}{2}}}{4}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (- \frac{9 e^{- \frac{3 x}{2}}}{4})\,\text{d}x \\ y & =- \frac{9}{4}\int e^{- \frac{3 x}{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =- \frac{9}{4}\left(- \frac{2 e^{- \frac{3 x}{2}}}{3}\right)+C \\ y & =\frac{3 e^{- \frac{3 x}{2}}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-2,0,2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186096698/plots/ee6a1ee91c08e1f1f700460cddd76cf16b4be486422c007af5e37ebcfcf0e090.png)
